strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Existing headless.run.drive returns an authoritative runtime-derived completion closure for caller next-action decisions.
The closure is derived in Rust from bounded runtime state, not VSIX or caller policy.
Replay uses existing drive checkpoints and bounded evidence without duplicating raw ledger data.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive includes completion_closure with complete, routed explicit action, budget exhausted, stale/no-progress, task-in-progress, no-eligible, and unknown nonterminal classifications.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Stop reasons, terminal completion evidence, and progress route candidates are separate surfaces and leave completion policy caller-owned.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Scheduled callers cannot reliably distinguish true completion from a route boundary or budget stop without wrapper summaries.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M32-M34 added recovery context, parent-join routing, and route candidate progress; M35.1 classifies drive closure.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.run.drive result is extended.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. No separate report/history/digest/readiness surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime derives and returns a bounded completion closure after drive execution and replay.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can choose continue, escalate, or close directly from the drive result.
answers.milestone_progress: This is the first and likely sufficient M35 vertical slice for a headless completion boundary.

exit_criteria: Completion is reported only when known applicable work is terminal and no explicit route remains.
Explicit route boundaries, budget exhaustion, stale progress, and task-in-progress never report completion.
Replay returns the same completion_closure without duplicate ledger events.
VSIX validators accept valid closure payloads and reject malformed fingerprints and raw fields.
No new RPC or wrapper surface is added.
